facts.text: Watervliet was founded in 1788, originally encompassing all of present‑day Albany County except the city of Albany.
The town’s name comes from Dutch “watervliet,” meaning “flats by the water,” and it became a city in 1896.
In 1813 the War of 1812 prompted the creation of the Watervliet Arsenal, the only U.S. facility that still manufactures large‑caliber cannon.
The North Reformed Dutch Church, built in 1839, now houses the Watervliet Historical Society and Museum at 1501 First Avenue.
The Albany and Northern Railway linked Watervliet to Albany in 1852, with a depot originally on Genesee Street before moving to Canal Street.
During the Revolutionary War, a ferry operated from Bleeker Farm across the Hudson to Troy, used by troops in 1777 en route to Saratoga.
